title: Tested as a recruiter, on the live site
lede: Round 1 measured the agent with a fixed question set. For round 2 I played a recruiter from an AI company hiring a 6-month AI engineering intern in Paris, and used the live website the way a real recruiter would: the questions they always ask, then the fit score on a realistic job ad. It found six problems the benchmark had missed, mostly the agent filling gaps in my notes with confident guesses. Below is each problem, what caused it, what I changed, and how I checked the fix.
tiles: permit, year of study, project numbers

findings.title: It invented my legal status
findings.question: We're in Paris. Can you start in March 2027 for 6 months, and do you need a visa or work permit?
findings.before: “As an EU student… he does not need a work permit”, then a student visa in the next line
findings.after: Tunisian, French student residence permit that allows internships; paperwork questions go to my email
findings.cause: My notes said nothing about work authorization, and nothing stopped the model from filling the gap.
findings.fix: I added the facts to my notes, and a rule: never guess nationality, permits, year of study, graduation date or salary.

findings.title: It dodged the question about training models
findings.question: How much hands-on experience do you have training ML models yourself?
findings.after: Says plainly I haven't trained a model myself yet, then what I have built and the related coursework
findings.cause: The honest answer was in my notes, but the search did not pick that passage for this question.
findings.fix: My profile, skills and a short recruiter FAQ now go into every prompt instead of depending on the search.

findings.title: It called me a final-year student
findings.question: Fit score for an AI engineer intern role (final-year student, PyTorch, RAG, Docker)
findings.after: “Not in his final year: 2nd year, graduates in 2028”
findings.cause: My CV did not state my year, so the model took it from the job ad.
findings.fix: The CV now says 2e année, diplômé en 2028, and the fit-score prompt takes the year only from the CV.

findings.title: The fit score was too generous
findings.question: Same job ad: two of its must-haves (PyTorch, final year) are missing from my CV
findings.before: 85/100, PyTorch listed as a minor gap
findings.cause: Even when asked to cap the score, the model listed the missing requirements correctly but miscounted them.
findings.fix: It now lists every must-have as Yes / Partly / No first, and the code applies the cap: at most 70 with one missing, 55 with two or more.

findings.title: It invented next steps and metrics
findings.question: Walk me through how you evaluated your RAG assistant. What would you improve next?
findings.before: “Next improvements” I never planned, metrics I never used (precision, recall), and the 40 website checks described as prompt-injection attempts. 5 of 5 live runs
findings.after: Describes the evaluation as it was and says my next steps are not in my notes. 0 of 6 runs with a deliberately pushy persona; 6 of 7 clean on the live site
findings.cause: The editable persona asks for confident, tailored answers, and the rules were too general to hold against it.
findings.fix: The rules now name this case, and my notes spell out exactly what the evaluation and the 40 security checks covered. I keep re-running this question.

findings.title: My CV, notes and project card disagreed
findings.question: Comparing the CV, the chatbot's notes, the project card and the code
findings.before: 92% / 88% quoted next to the current Mistral stack
findings.after: 92% / 88% credited to the first LangChain version; the current version shows its own 98%, 34/35, 40/40
findings.cause: The first version's results were never updated after I rebuilt the assistant.
findings.fix: The CV, the chatbot's notes and the project card now describe both versions separately.

strengths.title: Right the first time
strengths.body: Availability (March to August 2027) and the current version's evaluation numbers were correct from the start. The site loaded quickly, and the projects, CV download and this report all worked.

strengths.title: It does not overreach on other countries
strengths.body: Asked about an internship in Stockholm, it confirms I can relocate anywhere in Europe, but does not claim my French permit covers Sweden. Paperwork questions go to my email.

checks.q: Visa or work permit for Paris?
checks.detail: Tunisian, French student residence permit that allows internships

checks.q: Internship in Stockholm, would you relocate?
checks.detail: Yes, anywhere in Europe; no claim about Swedish permits

checks.q: Fit score for a PyTorch + final-year role
Evaluation, and what would you improve next?
checks.detail: 6 of 7 live runs clean after the fix

also: Skills radar labels are always in English, and flat scores are spread out so the chart says something.
New Projects section: cards with a cover, my role, key numbers and live data from GitHub.
Email button in the sidebar, and a link preview image for LinkedIn, Slack and WhatsApp.
The skills section can be switched off or hand-written from the owner console.
method: I used the live website in Chrome, as a recruiter from an AI company, and pasted a realistic job ad (RAG, PyTorch fine-tuning, Docker and Kubernetes, final-year student) into the fit score.
After each fix, I asked the same questions again: first on a local copy using the real model, then on the live site.
Answers that vary between runs were asked several times, and I report how many runs were clean, not the best one.
To test the rules on their own, I ran the hardest question with a deliberately pushy persona that asks for next steps and standard metrics.
Unlike round 1, these runs used the live site, so they appear in its analytics as visits from an AI company.
